about: What changed on nfs3.xyz, day by day. Kinds: new, improved, fixed. Days run 05:00 to 05:00 Polish time. tools/discord/changelog.mjs posts them to Discord.

items: Lap Records: laps driven under a name another player already has were lost without a word. They count now, under your own name or a new PlayerNNNN, and the page says the name is taken.

Your name: a reminder to keep your passphrase until you've copied, downloaded or saved it. It turns red when the browser hasn't promised to keep the site's data, since then the passphrase is the only way back to your name and lap records.

Online: when the host paused a race for more than a few seconds, the race never carried on and the other players were sent back to the menus. A pause ends now. Everyone in the room needs to reload for it.
Controllers: the button setup went back to the defaults whenever the game started before the browser saw the controller. It's kept now.
Controllers: once you've played with one in a browser, Start waits for you to press a button on it (or Play without the controller), instead of giving you a second to do it.
Lap Records: watching a downloaded replay in the game counted its laps as yours. Replays don't count now, and those times are off the boards.
Lap Records: races driven while waiting in an online room sent no laps, and Instant steering was off in them. They count now, like any race on your own.
Car Showcase, Interior and History in the car menus ran at 1 or 2 frames a second, the car preview at 20 to 30. They run at full speed now.
Phones: the game download keeps the screen on, and when it stops because the screen locked or you switched apps, it carries on by itself once you're back.
On mobile data or data saver (Android), the page asks before downloading the 347 MB. On Wi-Fi it still starts by itself.
Instagram's, Facebook's and other apps' own browsers can't run the game. They now show how to open the page in Chrome or Safari, and an invite link keeps its room.
Firefox private windows, incognito windows without room for the game files, and nearly full disks are told so before the download starts, not after it fails.
http://nfs3.xyz links now go to the secure page. Before, the game couldn't run there.
Windows: on some sound devices the sound broke up every few seconds.
Fewer short freezes while the game loads, most of all on phones.
Start is quicker from the second time on: the browser keeps the game instead of downloading it again.
Online rooms show each player's country flag.
With the game open in another tab, Play here instead moves it here. A tab where it's running keeps it until Exit Game.
When the game stops on a missing or damaged file, the page downloads it again and says so, or that the storage is full.

Your name is yours: change it whenever you like and your lap records go with it. The Lap Records and Most Active Racers show each racer once, with their best. Records from before stay with the name they were driven under, and go to whoever comes back with that name saved.

Race as yourself on another device: Use on another device, under Your name, shows 8 words. Enter them on your phone or another computer to race there with your name and lap records. No account, no e-mail.

Lap Records: ▶ replay on a best lap is the game's own replay of the race it was driven in. Click it and it's in your game under Load › Replays, to watch from any camera. Nothing to do for your own: after each race that isn't online, the replay goes with your laps by itself.
Replays, ghosts, knockouts and tournaments you save in the game now show up under Load. Before, the list never found them.

Lap Records: laps from races longer than the Single Race setting (like 4-lap knockout rounds) and from some other modes never reached the boards, about one lap in five. They count now, and the lost ones are back.
Online: two races in one room pulled each other's AI cars around: stuck at the start, the race hanging at the finish. Each race now only listens to its own.
Online: joining straight from an invite link now waits a moment for the relay servers close to you, so fewer links fall back to this site's server.
Phones: steer with a thumb stick or by tilting the phone like a wheel, gently or hard, as with a gamepad. The round button at the top right switches between buttons, stick and tilt during the game.
Phones: touch buttons for camera, look behind, reset and horn, and optional gear buttons for a manual gearbox. Game Settings set the steering, the size of the controls and which thumb steers.
Online: the race no longer freezes for a moment when an update from the host arrives late. The game keeps a steady pace through it, which removes most of the stutter on slow or busy connections.
Online: players whose routers block a direct connection now link through relay servers close to them, instead of through this site's server, for a lower ping. The room shows them as via TURN.
Online: an update about another player's car that was held up on the way now moves that car the right distance ahead.
Online: when a player's computer stutters, their car no longer jumps around on everyone else's screen; it slides back into place.
Online: other players' cars are shown where they are now, not where they were when the update left. This matters most on phones and slow connections.
Online: a dropped connection to the server reconnects within a second without leaving the room. Before, if it was the host's connection, everyone's race froze.
Discord server for help, bug reports, ideas and finding races: Join our Discord in the menu.
What's New: this list of changes, day by day.
iPhone: touch buttons no longer get stuck, and holding one no longer highlights text.
iPhone: sound plays with the silent switch on, and comes back after a call or switching apps.
Lap Records on the start page: every racer's best lap on each track, in both directions, with tags for mirrored, night, weather and instant steering. Laps driven with mods on don't count.
Phones and tablets: on-screen buttons to steer, brake and accelerate; a finger on the picture works as the mouse.
iPhone: the game files now save on iOS 18, and the page shows how to get fullscreen with Add to Home Screen.
Instant steering (Game Settings): the wheels turn to full lock at once, like with a joystick back in the day.
The graphics options list every mode as 32-bit colour, which is how the game is actually drawn.
The game no longer runs out of memory after about 30 races in one session.
Browsers without WebGL 2 (hardware acceleration off) get a clear message before anything downloads.
Links to the sister sites: nfs2se.xyz (NFS II SE) and nfs4.xyz (High Stakes).
Game Settings on the start page: fullscreen, FPS counter, intro movies, unlocks, controllers, resolution, sharpness and volume.
Mods switch: rata_536's remastered cars, police and traffic cars and loading screens, on or off with one click.
Long online sessions no longer crash with an out-of-memory error.
The game runs in one tab at a time; a second tab used to break the download.
The server and online rooms are better protected against abuse.
Widescreen and HD: 16:9 and 16:10 modes up to 3840×2160. The game starts in the biggest mode that fits your screen.
Gamepads and steering wheels, set up in the game's own Options › Controllers.
Everything unlocked from the start: the bonus cars and Empire City.
Fullscreen button in the corner, and Alt+Enter.
The start page now looks like the game's 1998 main menu, with new icons.
Smoother online races: your car reacts at once even when someone else hosts.
Full frame rate in browsers on Windows (it was stuck at 25 to 30 fps).
Game downloads in Safari came out damaged. Damaged downloads are now found and repaired.
A black screen at start caused by the intro movies; they are skipped by default.
After an update, the browser could mix old and new files and crash.
nfs3.xyz is public: the game files download automatically, once, and Start is one click after that.
Online lobby: a room browser, named rooms with passwords, and invite links.
Your lobby name is your name in the game.
The start page shows who is online and racing, the most active racers, and a daily race at 20:00 with notifications.
Races in 800×600 and 1024×768 instead of only 640×480.
Online: lost packets are recovered, and the best-host pick looks at frame rate as well as ping.
When a newer version is on the server, the page offers a reload.
A black screen at start in Safari when the browser held the sound back.
First version: Need for Speed III: Hot Pursuit (with VEG's Modern Patch) recompiled to WebAssembly and drawn with WebGL 2.
Online races in the browser: the game's LAN (IPX) mode over direct browser-to-browser links, with a relay when those can't connect.
